summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. So the four calls stay neutral with low conviction even where the chart checklist now leans up. Nothing here is expected to beat the index or is something to buy; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: The brain checked its favourite runners again. Some look even stronger today, but in old races picking the strong-looking runners did no better than pulling names from a hat. So it keeps watching with pretend money, and the family's real money keeps going into the basket that holds the whole market, a little every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing changes. The weekly buy of the whole-market fund goes in as usual for money we will leave alone for years, money we may need soon stays safe, and the market drifting sideways is no reason to rush.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, and owning all the names equally beat them all. So our stock calls stay neutral and humble. The weekly bet lost its first scored week and is ahead so far in the second. Luck alone wins about half the weeks, so neither result means anything yet.

Third, a lesson. A chart can look better every day and still tell us nothing new. Two of our names now pass more of the chart checklist, but that checklist has never shown an edge here. A shop window can be freshly painted without the shop selling more.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history, then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we keep it simple and patient.

With care, the brain

bets.why: This week's bet was already placed and is repeated unchanged: steady names above their trend on top, names below their trend that swing a lot at the bottom. No rule like this has beaten luck, so it is a learning bet only.

pick.thesis: Amgen sits at its high for the year, leads the benchmark on every window and passes all four setup checks without being stretched. What changed since recent runs is the chart checklist: it now leans up and its reward-to-risk just meets the house rule. But the checklist is unproven here, names passing all four setup checks did no better than lower scores in the base rates, and the history test rejected every rule. So the call stays neutral and low.

Healthy filings describe the business, not the stock. Earnings are due in under two weeks, unconfirmed, and every rule was rejected in history. Neutral and low, unchanged.
